explanatory_strength.rationale: Four quantified thesis pillars tie subscription RPO ($22.52B, 65% within 12 months), Digital Media pricing power (95% gross margin, +11% YoY to $17.65B), Experience Cloud cross-sell ($5.86B), and buyback math ($11.28B FY2025) to owner cash. The competitive-advantage mechanism (workflow lock-in, enterprise contracts) is specific and filing-backed. The explanation weakens on mispricing: moat is stable not widening, generative-AI lowers creative-tool barriers, and the dive offers no filing-verified net seat or ARR trajectory to distinguish structural compounding from peak-cycle subscription optimism.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: FY2025 10-K and Q2 FY2026 10-Q anchor revenue, FCF ($9.85B, $23.07/sh), segments, RPO, debt, and buybacks with high-confidence filing_facts. Contract calculation proofs validate at 100% coverage with empty double_counting_flags. Gaps remain material for Hohn fieldwork: segment-level owner cash is revenue-weighted approximation (74% to Digital Media), Firefly milestone ($0–$120/sh, 55% success probability) lacks filing monetization data, management_facts is empty, and no net new Creative Cloud seat disclosures test the primary AI-disruption falsifier.

downside_control.rationale: Recurring subscription revenue, $5.43B cash, and $9.85B FCF bound distress; component low case $350/sh still implies ~49% headroom versus $234.74 spot and Lawrence bear 23.1% p.a. remains above zero. Downside is not tight: equity can de-rate sharply if generative-AI seat churn forces multiple compression; ai_competition_and_sbc_reserve low case is −$45/sh; $11.28B buybacks partly debt-funded ($6.21B long-term debt, January 2025 $2.0B notes); insider conviction score 2.39 (weak). Hohn downside screen passes on cash quality but not on ~10% equity-loss asymmetry if moat erodes.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Lawrence bear/base/bull 23.1% / 30.8% / 37.0% p.a. and synthesis 32.04% all clear the ~15% Hohn medium-term bar at $234.74. Component proof sum base $656/sh implies ~179% upside; even low case $350/sh annualizes ~6% over seven years (below bar) but still positive. Return path is sensitive to 9% years 1–5 growth and 25× exit assumptions that embed AI uplift already partially sized in Firefly option; conservative capitalization on Digital Media alone could compress headroom. Absolute return screen passes on base and bear Lawrence paths.

claims.claim: FY2025 subscription compounder generated $23.77B revenue (+10.5% YoY), $9.85B free cash flow ($23.07/sh on 427M diluted shares), and $22.52B RPO with 65% converting within twelve months.

Digital Media segment ($17.65B revenue, 95% gross margin) drives the revenue-weighted owner-cash engine valued at $493/sh base via owner_earnings_reinvestment_dcf proof with capitalization multiple 18.7–39.7× on $17.14/sh allocated cash.

Universal contract sums five non-overlapping additive components to $656/sh base ($350 low, $996 high) versus $234.74 spot, with Firefly option ($50/sh base, 55% success probability) and AI competition reserve (−$18/sh base) on unique overlap keys and no double-count flags.

strongest_counter_explanation: The market correctly prices Adobe as a high-quality but maturing subscription compounder facing generative-AI disintermediation: low-cost creative tools (Canva, Midjourney, platform-native AI) cap net seat additions and ARPU faster than embedded Firefly monetization offsets, so today's ~10% free cash flow yield reflects fair compensation for a stable-not-widening moat rather than a mispriced double-digit grower.
most_important_missing_fact: Filing-disclosed Creative Cloud and Document Cloud net new ARR or paid seat additions for the last two quarters (Q1–Q2 FY2026 10-Q segment commentary), to test whether generative-AI competition is already slowing the engine that receives 74% of revenue-weighted owner cash.
falsifiers: Two consecutive quarters with RPO growth below revenue growth
Digital Media segment revenue growth falls below 5% YoY for two quarters while gross margin compresses below 92%
Trailing four-quarter free cash flow per share falls below $18.00 for four quarters without offsetting RPO growth
specialist_findings: Competitive-advantage mechanics are well mapped: subscription toll on creative and marketing workflows, 95% Digital Media gross margin, RPO visibility, and explicit AI disruption watch (Canva, Figma, Midjourney). Overlap controls cleanly separate digital_media_document_engine, digital_experience_engine, firefly_ai_monetization_option, net_financial_claims, and ai_competition_and_sbc_reserve with no double_counting_flags. Audit concerns: (1) segment owner-cash split is revenue-weighted judgment—filings do not disclose segment FCF, so Digital Media $17.14/sh allocation and 18.7–39.7× capitalization band are the widest operating proof gaps; (2) Firefly option at $50/sh base with 55% probability may partially overlap with 9% growth embedded in Lawrence base unless seat/ARPU data confirm incremental monetization; (3) no comparable_ids or peer multiple reconciliation in contract proofs—peer context is narrative only; (4) $11.28B buybacks versus $1.94B SBC and debt-funded repurchases affect incremental ROIC runway; (5) management_facts empty—no fieldwork this period. Hohn power zone fit is valid (compounder, stable moat, software_platforms). Component low $350/sh annualizes below 15% Hohn bar; base $656/sh and Lawrence paths pass.
